label: RSA-2048
description: Broken by Shor's algorithm. NIST targets deprecation by 2030.

label: RSA-3072
description: Broken by Shor's algorithm. Extended deprecation timeline over RSA-2048.

label: RSA-4096
description: Broken by Shor's algorithm. Larger key provides no quantum resistance.

label: ECDSA P-256
description: Broken by Shor's algorithm. Used widely in TLS and code signing.

label: ECDSA P-384
description: Broken by Shor's algorithm.

label: ECDSA P-521
description: Broken by Shor's algorithm. Highest NIST curve.

label: ECDH P-256
description: ECDH on P-256 curve. Key agreement is vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. Some transition profiles use a classical + PQC hybrid; the applicable protocol and authority determine whether that construction is allowed or required.

label: ECDH P-384
description: ECDH on P-384 curve. Key agreement is vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. Some transition profiles use a classical + PQC hybrid; the applicable protocol and authority determine whether that construction is allowed or required.

label: ECDH P-521
description: ECDH on P-521 curve. Key agreement is vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. Some transition profiles use a classical + PQC hybrid; the applicable protocol and authority determine whether that construction is allowed or required.

label: Ed25519
description: Used in SSH, Solana. Vulnerable to quantum attack.

label: Ed448
description: EdDSA on Curve448. Vulnerable to quantum attack.

label: DH (Diffie-Hellman)
description: Classic key exchange is vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. Some transition profiles use a classical + PQC hybrid; the applicable protocol and authority determine whether that construction is allowed or required.

label: AES-128
description: The ideal Grover key-search estimate is about 2^64 sequential iterations. NIST IR 8547 §4.1.3 places approved primitives with 128 bits of classical strength at least at Category 1. For National Security Systems under CNSA 2.0, use AES-256.

label: AES-192
description: The ideal Grover key-search estimate is about 2^96 sequential iterations. Check the required deployment profile.

label: AES-256
description: AES-256 is NIST’s Category 5 key-search reference. The ideal estimate of about 2^128 sequential queries is a separate model.

label: SHA-256
description: Finding a preimage for a chosen SHA-256 digest and finding any collision are different tasks. NIST’s Category 2 benchmark uses collision search on a 256-bit hash.

label: SHA-3
description: Check the SHA-3 variant, output length and required property. NIST uses SHA3-256 and SHA3-384 collision search as two category references.

label: 3DES
description: Already deprecated for classical security reasons. Migrate immediately.

label: ChaCha20-Poly1305
description: Symmetric stream cipher. Quantum-safe at current key sizes.

label: HMAC-SHA256
description: MAC function. Not affected by quantum computers.

label: X25519
description: Curve25519 key exchange. Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. Widely used in TLS 1.3; hybrid mode already deployed in Chrome/Firefox.

label: X448
description: Curve448 key exchange. Vulnerable to Shor's algorithm.

label: secp256k1
description: Used in Bitcoin/Ethereum. Vulnerable to quantum attack.

label: ML-KEM-512
description: FIPS 203 (2024). NIST Level 1 KEM. Quantum-safe key encapsulation.

label: ML-KEM-768
description: FIPS 203 (2024). NIST Level 3 KEM. Recommended default for most applications.

label: ML-KEM-1024
description: FIPS 203 (2024). NIST Level 5 KEM. Highest security level.

label: ML-DSA-44
description: FIPS 204 (2024). NIST Level 2 digital signature. Replaces ECDSA P-256 / Ed25519.

label: ML-DSA-65
description: FIPS 204 (2024). NIST Level 3 digital signature. Replaces ECDSA P-384 / RSA-3072.

label: ML-DSA-87
description: FIPS 204 (2024). NIST Level 5 digital signature. Replaces RSA-4096.

label: SLH-DSA-128
description: FIPS 205 (2024). Stateless hash-based signature. Conservative fallback to ML-DSA.

label: SLH-DSA-192
description: FIPS 205 (2024). NIST Level 3 hash-based signature.

label: SLH-DSA-256
description: FIPS 205 (2024). NIST Level 5 hash-based signature.

label: LMS/HSS
description: SP 800-208 (2020). Stateful hash-based signature for firmware/boot. Requires strict state management.

label: XMSS/XMSS^MT
description: RFC 8391 (2018). Stateful hash-based signature. Used in specialized firmware signing.
